trigger: Signup, no paid plan
subject: Your first UGC ad in about 3 minutes
preheader: One product line, one hook, one presenter. Here is the order to do it in.
heading: Your first UGC ad in about 3 minutes
body_html:
Hi {{name}},

The quickest way to judge Vooads is to make one ad. Here is the order that works:

  1. Write one clear product line. What it is and who it is for. "Lightweight sunscreen with no white cast, for daily wear" beats "best sunscreen ever".
  2. Pick a hook that names a daily problem. For example: "I was tired of paying for apps I never opened."
  3. Choose a presenter, a language and 9:16. Then generate.

Tip: Make 3 versions with 3 different hooks. Same product, same offer, different first line. The hook decides who stops scrolling.

Want to see it first? The Learn tab in the studio has a 3-minute video called "Your first UGC video".

You have {{credits}} credits. Trial credits cover hooks and images. UGC videos come with any paid plan.

trigger: Signup, no paid plan
subject: How to get 50+ test creatives a week without a production team
preheader: A weekly routine for media buyers who need fresh ads in every ad set.
heading: A weekly creative routine that keeps up
body_html:
Hi {{name}},

Here is a pattern most media buyers know. You order a handful of creator videos, wait a week or two, one of them works, and by the time it fatigues the creative budget is gone.

The fix is more tests, cheaper and faster. Here is a routine you can run with Vooads. Treat it as an example and adjust it to your account.

  • Monday: Write 20 hooks for one product. Keep the best 10.
  • Tuesday: Turn your best 3 to 5 hooks into UGC videos. Use 2 presenters.
  • Wednesday: Make image sets and a slideshow version of the same angles.
  • Thursday: Give your best video new openings with a hook remix: same creator and body, a new first line.
  • Friday: Launch, read the data, cut losers, give winners more budget.

A mix of UGC videos, images, slideshows and hook remixes is how a Pro plan reaches 50+ creatives a week. Fifty brand-new UGC videos a week is a bigger plan, and we will tell you that straight.

Keep real creators for the big brand moments. Use Vooads for the volume testing that finds your winners.

heading: Plans, explained simply
body_html:
Hi {{name}},

Every plan includes monthly credits. Credits pay for videos, images, hooks and copy. You can top up any time.

  • Starter: For solo buyers testing a few products. UGC videos, static ads in every Meta size, hooks, copy and Ban Shield.
  • Pro: For buyers who test every week. Everything in Starter, more credits, and AI script writing. Give Vooads a product and an angle and get full UGC scripts ready to generate.
  • Scale and Agency: For teams and agencies. More credits, longer product videos and a better price per credit.

Not sure? Start with Pro. Scripts are where most buyers save the most time. You can switch plans any time.

All plans include commercial use, no watermark and 20+ languages. Pay by card, local methods or USDT/BTC.

trigger: Signup, no paid plan
subject: Example: one buyer, one product, one week of tests
preheader: A walkthrough of how a media buyer could use Vooads on a single product. An example, not a result.
heading: A worked example: one product, one week
body_html:
Hi {{name}},

This is an example walkthrough, not a customer story. It shows how a media buyer could use Vooads on one product in one week, with real credit costs.

The setup: a buyer runs a sunscreen offer on Meta in two markets, English and Spanish. One ad is live and starting to fatigue.

Day 1: angles. They generate a hook pack for each of 3 angles: no white cast, works in heat, and one step instead of three. That is 3 packs at 6 credits each (18 credits).

Day 2: videos. They pick the 4 strongest hooks and make 15-second UGC videos with 2 presenters. That is 8 videos at 225 credits each, 1,800 credits.

Day 3: statics. 5 image sets in all three Meta sizes (60 credits).

Day 4: Ban Shield. Every script was already checked. They also paste their primary text and headline before launch.

Day 5: launch and read. New ads go into the account next to the old winner. After a few days they keep what holds and cut what does not.

Week 2: next market. The angle that held gets a native Spanish script and a presenter who fits that market.

Total for the week: about 1,880 credits. That fits inside a Pro month with room to spare. Your numbers will differ. The point is the routine: test angles first, hooks second, presenters third, markets fourth.

trigger: Signup, no paid plan
subject: The honest answers to the 5 questions buyers ask us
preheader: Will it look fake? Will my ads get banned? Who owns the videos? Straight answers.
heading: Straight answers to fair questions
body_html:
Hi {{name}},

These are the questions we get most from media buyers before they pay. Here are honest answers.

1. Will it look like AI? Sometimes. Presenter quality is good and keeps improving, but a sharp viewer can spot AI on some frames. Test it next to your current creatives and let your numbers decide. Platforms also label realistic AI content, so switch on the AI disclosure setting where your platform asks for it.

2. Will Ban Shield stop rejections? It lowers the risk. It flags income claims, health claims, personal attributes and other common triggers. It cannot guarantee approval. The platforms make the final call.

3. Who owns what I make? On a paid plan you can use your outputs commercially, including in paid ads, with no watermark. Trial outputs are for testing only.

4. What if a render fails? You get the credits back.

5. What if it is not for me? New plans can be refunded within 7 days if you used less than 10% of the credits. Top-ups never expire, and unused ones can be refunded within 7 days.

Any question not on this list? Reply to this email.

trigger: Signup, no paid plan
subject: A note from the person who built Vooads
preheader: Why it exists, what it is good at, and what it is not.
heading: Why I built Vooads
body_html:
Hi {{name}},

I am Ejiro, founder of Vooads. I run paid traffic myself, with a team of media buyers, and Vooads came out of that work.

Our problem was simple. Winning ads died fast, and new creatives took too long and cost too much. We needed more hooks, more presenters and more languages every week, and we could not get them from creators at the speed we were testing.

So we built the tool we wanted. It is good at volume: hooks, scripts, UGC videos, image sets and local versions, quickly, with a policy check on every script.

Here is what it is not. It does not replace a great real creator for a big brand moment. It does not guarantee your ads get approved or that they will win. Nothing does. It gives you more shots, faster, so your data can find the winner.

One more thing I care about: we do not want scammers on Vooads. If someone uses it for fake giveaways, impersonation or guaranteed-return schemes, we ban the account without a refund. That protects the honest buyers, and it protects the ad platforms we all rely on.

If you tried Vooads and it did not fit, I would like to know why. Reply to this email. I read the replies.

Ejiro
Founder, Vooads

trigger: Long video job (more than one segment) finishes
subject: Your {{seconds}}s video is ready
preheader: All parts are rendered and joined. Download it from your library.
heading: Your long video is ready
body_html:
Hi {{name}},

Your {{seconds}}-second video is done. It was rendered in {{segments}} parts with the same presenter and voice, then joined into one file.

Before you launch:

  • Watch it once with sound and once on mute. The captions should carry the message on their own.
  • Check the joins between parts. If one feels abrupt, trim it in your editor or render that length again.
  • Consider cutting a 15 or 30-second version from the same script. Test both lengths.

If a long render ever fails, every credit for it goes back to your balance automatically.
